description: Imports a block in SimaticML XML (the only path for LAD/FBD/GRAPH — Gd6). PREFER `xml` inline (tested up to ~300 KB: 280 KB imported in 1–5 s); use `path` ONLY for a file that is already on the serve host — never copy files to the host to import them. Gd7: SimaticML version must match V21. Import UDTs FIRST (tia_types_import). Returns, per block, type/number/created/interfaceChanged/affectedInstanceDbs, and — when `xml` was sent inline — a transport check (sha256 sent vs received). Requires app ≥ v1.6.0 for the receipt; with an older serve transport.match is null and there are no per-block fields. An FB whose interface changed makes the next compile regenerate its instance DBs. Stale-write guard: pass the block's `contentHash` from tia_export_block as `expectedContentHash` and the serve checks it against the block's current export BEFORE importing — a mismatch is 409 state_changed and NOTHING is imported; a match adds `contentGuard` to the result. `contentHash`, `normalizedSha256` and `sha256` are different hash contracts over different normalizations: never substitute one for another, and pass only the `contentHash` of a fresh read as `expectedContentHash`. It guards exactly ONE block: the XML (or the file at `path`) must contain exactly one block (else 400 bad_request), and a hash for a block that does not exist (any more) is refused as state_changed — omit it to create. The guard never compiles: a block that is not consistent is refused with 409 inconsistent (compile, re-read with tia_export_block, retry), and one whose current export is not well-formed XML cannot be hashed and is refused with 409 unverifiable (NOTHING is imported; repair it, or omit expectedContentHash to write without the guard). Needs an app with the guard: an older serve ignores the field and the result says the import was NOT guarded. dryRun never verifies it. Maps to POST /plcs/{plc}/import. M-off.

dryRun.description: Gd11: plan-without-applying — validates the guards and describes the action WITHOUT mutating the project

expectedContentHash.description: Stale-write guard (optional): the `contentHash` of the object as you last read it (tia_export_block, tia_export_type or tia_type_source; 64 hex characters). `contentHash`, `normalizedSha256` and `sha256` are different hash contracts over different normalizations: never substitute one for another, and pass only the `contentHash` of a fresh read as `expectedContentHash`. The serve compares it with the object's CURRENT hash inside the same operation, BEFORE writing, and refuses with 409 state_changed (nothing written) when it differs; a match is confirmed by `contentGuard` in the result. It guards exactly ONE object per write (the source must declare exactly one block or type, else 400 bad_request). A hash for an object that does not exist (any more) is refused as state_changed, so omit it when creating. The guard never compiles: an existing object that is not consistent is refused with 409 inconsistent and nothing written (compile, re-read with tia_export_block / tia_export_type, retry); one whose current export is not well-formed XML cannot be hashed and is refused with 409 unverifiable (nothing written; repair it, or omit expectedContentHash to write without the guard). Needs an app with the guard. dryRun does NOT verify it: the plan only shows it.

override.description: overwrite if it already exists (default true)

path.description: path to the .xml on the serve host (alternative to xml)
